# THE CORPORATION OF THE TOWNSHIP OF NIPISSING

## BY-LAW NUMBER 2019-41

*Being a By-Law to adopt Minimum Maintenance Standards for Municipal Highways*

*Unofficial consolidation incorporating By-law 2020-52 and By-law 2024-12.*

WHEREAS Section 44(1) of the Municipal Act, R.S.O. 2001, states that municipalities shall keep all highways and bridges under its jurisdiction in a state of repair that is reasonable in the circumstances including the character and location of the highway or bridge;

AND WHEREAS Section 44(4) of the Municipal Act, R.S.O. 2001, states that the Minister of Transportation may make regulations establishing minimum standards of repair for highways and bridges or any class of them;

AND WHEREAS the Minister has done so in Ontario Regulation 239/02 Minimum Maintenance Standards for Municipal Highways (MMS), by prescribing standards for Classes 1 through 6 highways, based on the speed limit applicable to it and the average daily traffic on it;

AND WHEREAS the Township of Nipissing passed By-Law Number 2013-39 authorizing the speed limit of sixty (60) kilometers per hour for all unpaved roads under its jurisdiction;

NOW THEREFORE the Council of The Corporation of the Township of Nipissing enacts as follows:

## Part 1 - Definitions

CITATION AND SCHEDULES: This By-Law shall be cited as the "Township of Nipissing Road Status and Maintenance By-Law".

Schedule A, being Ontario Regulation 239/02 and any amendment thereto, is hereby incorporated by reference into this By-Law.

Schedule B showing Public Roads, average annual daily vehicle counts and the Class of various roads is annexed to and forms part of this By-Law.

Schedule C being the Winter Operation Plan and Deployment Procedure for the Township of Nipissing, annexed to and forms part of this By-Law.

Schedule D being the Winter Patrol Procedures and Winter Patrol Records for the South and North Roads, annexed to and forms part of this By-Law.

Schedule E being the Winter Operations Plow Routes for the Township of Nipissing, annexed to and forms part of this By-Law.

Schedule F being the Winter Patrol roads for the Township of Nipissing, annexed to and forms part of this By-Law.

1.1 Public Road - means a "highway" within the meaning of the Municipal Act of Ontario, 2001, as amended, which is under the jurisdiction of the Township of Nipissing.

1.2 Public Road Allowance - means an allowance for a road surveyed by the original Crown surveyors of the Township or subsequently conveyed and dedicated as a Public Road that is located within the Township of Nipissing and which is recorded in the records of the Land Registry Office as being owned by the Corporation of the Township of Nipissing or the municipality having jurisdiction over such road allowance.

1.3 Private Road - means a road that is neither owned nor maintained by the municipality.

1.4 Significant Weather Event - means an approaching or occurring weather hazard with the potential to pose a significant danger to users of the highways within a municipality.

1.5 Weather Hazard - means the weather hazards determined by Environment Canada as meeting the criteria for the issuance of an alert under its Public Weather Alerting Program.

## Part 2 - General

2.1 ROAD CLASSIFICATION: Public Roads within the Township shall be classified as per Schedule A, based on the following two factors:

a. Maximum speed limit - as defined by the Township's Speed Limit on Municipal Roads By-Law 2013-39.

b. Vehicle Use - as defined by the Average Annual Daily Traffic (AADT), counted once every five (5) years by the Township. For roads with high seasonal vehicle use, AADT will be counted in both the summer months and in the off-season, and assigned the more restrictive class based on the higher of the two traffic counts.

2.2 POLICY PRINCIPLES: In carrying out its responsibilities to maintain Public Roads and bridges, the Township will adhere to the following:

a. Operational activities of the Roads Department shall be directed to maintain the Township's Public Roads to the prescribed standards herein. Care shall be taken first to assure that the standards of the MMS are maintained and secondly that such services are efficiently and effectively rendered.

b. Neither this Township nor its officials make any promises or assurance that Public Roads or any Public Road in particular will be maintained in excess of the minimum standards herein defined now or in the future. The fact that the Township may, and indeed hopes, to exceed those standards, when the resources available permit it to do so, does not change the standards prescribed herein.

c. The standards and road classifications shall be made publicly available to ratepayers and other users of the municipal road network. Council will review concerns about the standards and their implementation within a reasonable time when they are brought to its attention.

d. Budgets and Council priorities shall be set on the basis that the minimum maintenance standards prescribed herein must be met.

e. Where the Township is asked to upgrade the maintenance standards of a particular Public Road, it will generally do so on the basis that the average annual daily usage of the road has significantly increased and places it in a higher Class as prescribed in Schedule A.

f. Where the Township is asked to accept a Private Road into the municipal road system, and agrees in principle to do so, it will generally require the proponents to first bring the road to specified standards as to design, roadbed, and surface, at the proponents' own expense.

2.4 SIGNIFICANT WEATHER EVENT: When a Weather Hazard occurs that meets the criteria for the issuance of an alert under the Public Weather Alerting Program by Environment Canada, the Operations Superintendent or Designate shall monitor the weather. (O. Reg 239/02 (4.1))

The Operations Superintendent or Designate shall have the designated authority to declare a significant weather event and deploy the public works crew as soon as practicable with regard to public and staff safety. If a Significant Weather Event is declared, the Operations Superintendent or Designate shall ensure that a Declaration Notice to advise the public of the nature of the event and expected service alteration is completed and published.

The Operations Superintendent or Designate shall continue to monitor the weather and when practicable, declare the end of the event with the completion of an End of Declared Notice being completed and published.

For the purposes of 2.4 of this By-Law, the Declared Notice and End of Declared Notice shall be completed and published the following ways:

a. Posting on the Township website, social media pages in use and CodeRed.

{{amended: 2024-12 | 2.4(a) replaced with new wording}}

b. [Deleted]

{{deleted: 2024-12}}

c. Circulation of the notice to the Nipissing Fire Department, Parry Sound Emergency Medical Services, North Bay Central Ambulance Communication Centre and the Ontario Provincial Police, Northeastern.

By-Law Number 2008-1218 is hereby repealed.

## SCHEDULE C

**By-Law 2019-41 – Township of Nipissing Road Status and Maintenance**

### Winter Operation Plan and Deployment Procedure

The purpose of this Plan and Procedure is to provide Public Works staff with a complete understanding of the Winter Operations methodology and expectations for the Township of Nipissing.

The Operations Superintendent has the authority to implement this procedure when they have determined it is required. In the absence of the Operations Superintendent, the Foreman will be deemed to have designated authority as required.

**Winter Seasons**

Shall start November 15th of each year and ends April 15th of the following year. Winter crews shall be on call between these months. Patrol may be suspended or re-scheduled in accordance with weather requirements by the Operations Superintendent or designate.

{{amended: 2024-12 | sentence added on suspending or re-scheduling patrol}}

Notwithstanding the generally understood winter season time frame, abnormal and severe weather events have been occurring at unexpected intervals and staff will be expected to respond when needed as is practicable.

**Winter Sand**

Shall be mixed with 3% salt and stacked in sand dome by August 1st to ensure time to drain excess moisture from the sand.

**Equipment**

The Township shall have 3 tandem plow wing sander trucks, one grader with wing tower and a 1-ton pick-up truck with snow plow and sander. Equipment shall be ready to go into service no later than November 1st.

Winter maintenance equipment may be removed from the equipment any time after March 31st as instructed by the Operations Superintendent.

**Routes**

Each piece of equipment shall have an assigned route to plow/sand. When sand truck operators finish their routes, they shall assist with the sanding of the grader route as required.

1-ton truck shall plow/sand Township Office, Fire Station 1/Community Centre/Fitness Centre and Fire Station 2 yards.

Winter Operations Plow Routes map attached as Schedule E to the Township of Nipissing Road Status and Maintenance By-Law. Where routes will be followed, equipment may be changed in response to the severity of the occurrence or the nature of the work to be performed, such as the winging back of the snow banks. The Operations Superintendent or designate will have the authority to make those required changes.

**Call outs**

Winter crews shall be mobilized within an hour of call out time.

**End of shift**

Trucks and equipment shall be fueled and ready to return to service after each plow run.
Truck and equipment shall be washed within 24 hours of last use.
Sander chains shall be visually inspected after each run.
Plow equipment shall be left in heated garage when not in use.

**Maintenance**

Truck and equipment shall be greased weekly and checked for any problems by each operator. Problems or concerns regarding trucks or equipment or the efficiency/safety of same, shall be reported to the Operations Superintendent immediately. In the absence of the Operations Superintendent, the Foreman shall be considered to have full authority and act in the Operations Superintendent's place.

## SCHEDULE D

**By-Law 2019-41 – Township of Nipissing Road Status and Maintenance**

### Winter Patrol Procedures

- Winter equipment shall be ready November 1st.
- Winter patrol shall start November 15th and shall end April 15th. *In the event of a winter weather event outside of these dates, Winter Patrol Procedures shall be provided until road conditions are considered acceptable.
- Patrol rotation shall start on Thursday and finish on Wednesday each week.

  {{amended: 2024-12 | Point 3: rotation now Thursday to Wednesday}}
- Patroller shall drive to the shop each morning and pick up patrol truck.
- Patrol truck fuel tank shall never be left less than half tank of fuel.
- Patroller on duty shall start patrol at or before 4 am in response to weather conditions. The Operations Superintendent or designate may alter patrol start times at their discretion dependent on weather conditions, current and anticipated. *In the event of a winter weather event requiring winter maintenance operations, working hours may be extended past the scheduled shift as needed.

  {{amended: 2024-12 | Point 6: patrol start time and discretion to alter it}}
- Patroller on weekend duty shall do their 4-hour patrol and go home if no action is required.
- Patroller shall track time and date of all call outs on the corresponding Patrol Sheet.
- Patroller shall fill out daily Patrol Tablet. The Patrol Tablet are in two parts, breaking the total roads into groupings of north and south. Winter Patrol Tablet for North and South are attached to and form a part of this procedure. The Winter Patrol roads designated for North and South patrol areas are indicated on Schedule F, attached to and forming part of the Township of Nipissing Road Status and Maintenance By-Law.

  {{amended: 2024-12 | Point 9: three instances of "Patrol Sheets" replaced with "Patrol Tablet"}}
- Patroller shall patrol 10% of Township roads, with specific attention given to previously identified problem areas which are known to drift, have big hills and sharp corners, ensuring these areas are sufficiently evaluated.
- When a winter weather event occurs, the Patroller on call shall activate the winter crew once an accumulation of 5cm of snow or sleet is reached. When a winter weather event continues, roads shall be plowed and sanded every 10 hours until the event ends and roads are acceptable.
- When a winter event occurs in evening/night, the Patroller on call shall call the winter crew in as early as possible to begin plowing and sanding Township roads.
- Weather conditions will be completed each day by entering information into Patrol Tablet using the weather app in use. To be completed by the Patroller on duty.

  {{amended: 2024-12 | Point 13 replaced: weather conditions entered in Patrol Tablet}}

Schedules E and F are maps and cannot be reproduced as text. The Schedule E map attached to By-law 2020-52 is labelled 'By-law 2019-14' on its face, apparently a typo for 2019-41. The amending by-law itself refers correctly to 2019-41.

minimum-maintenance-standards.summary: This by-law sets the Township of Nipissing's minimum maintenance standards for municipal roads under Ontario Regulation 239/02. It classifies each public road, sets out how significant weather events are declared and publicized, and fixes winter operations and patrol procedures and routes. Amendments in 2020 and 2024 changed the plow-route map, the ways weather-event notices are published, and winter patrol scheduling and record-keeping.
